''Oroszlánok'' (Lions) | image = Kispest_Honvéd_FC_logo.svg | upright = 0.75 | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1909|8|3}} | ground = [[Bozsik Aréna]], [[Budapest]] | capacity = 8,200 | chairman = Tamás Leisztinger | Team Manager = | manager = [[Maurizio Jacobacci]] | league = [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|NB I]] | season = [[2025–26 Nemzeti Bajnokság II|2025–26]] | position = NB II, 2nd of 16 (promoted) | website = {{URL|honvedfc.hu}} | current = | pattern_la1 = _honved2223h | pattern_la2 = _macronwyverneco24wr | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b1 = _honved2223h | pattern_b2 = _macronwyverneco24wr | pattern_b3 = _macronshedir1yb | pattern_ra1 = _honved2223h | pattern_ra2 = _macronwyverneco24wr | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_sh2 = _macronskara2223wr | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so1 = | pattern_so2 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm1 = FF0000 | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | leftarm3 = FFFF00 | body1 = FF0000 | body2 = FFFFFF | body3 = FFFF00 | rightarm1 = FF0000 | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | rightarm3 = FFFF00 | shorts1 = 000000 | shorts2 = FFFFFF | shorts3 = FFFF00 | socks1 = 000000 | socks2 = FFFFFF | socks3 = FFFF00 }} '''Kispest-Honvéd Football Club''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈkiʃpɛʃt ˈhonveːd ˈɛft͡seː}}), commonly known as '''Kispest-Honvéd''' or simply '''Honvéd''', is a Hungarian [[sports club]] based in [[Kispest]], [[Budapest]], with the colours of red and black. The club is best known for its [[association football|football]] team. ''Honvéd'' means the Homeland Defence. Originally formed as ''Kispest AC'', they became ''Kispest FC'' in 1926 before reverting to their original name in 1944. The team enjoyed a golden age during the 1950s when it was renamed ''Budapesti Honvéd SE'' and became the [[Military of Hungary|Hungarian Army]] team. The club's top players from this era, [[Ferenc Puskás]], [[Sándor Kocsis]], [[József Bozsik]], [[Zoltán Czibor]], and [[Gyula Grosics]] helped the club win the [[Hungarian League]] four times during the 1950s and also formed the nucleus of the legendary [[Hungary national football team|Hungary national team]] popularly known as the ''[[Magical Magyars|Mighty Magyars]].'' During the 1980s and early 1990s, the club enjoyed another successful period, winning a further eight [[Hungarian League]] titles. They also won league and cup doubles in 1985 and 1989. In 1991, the club was renamed ''Kispest Honvéd FC'' and adopted its current name in 2003.{{Cite web|title=Budapest Honvéd {{!}} Hungarian Football|url=https://www.hungarianfootball.com/budapest-honved/|access-date=2021-10-11|website=HungarianFootball.com|language=en-GB|archive-date=7 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007142334/https://www.hungarianfootball.com/budapest-honved/|url-status=live}} When the club was originally formed in 1909, it also organised teams that competed in fencing, cycling, gymnastics, [[wrestling]], [[sport of athletics|athletics]], [[boxing]], and tennis. Later, the Honvéd family was extended to include a [[water polo]] team, now known as ''[[Budapesti Honvéd SE (men's water polo)|Groupama Honvéd]]'', a 33-times basketball-champion [[Budapesti Honvéd SE (men's basketball)|team]] and a [[Team Handball|handball]] team that were [[EHF Champions League|European Champions]] in 1982."}}
